falsifier: Any MWCC-1.2.5 function in which (a) a change to a LOCAL's declared type, declaration order or scope moves a PARAMETER's callee-saved register - which would show parameters and locals share one numbering partition; or (b) a K&R old-style definition produces object bytes that differ from the prototype-style definition of the same function - which would show the definition-form axis reaches codegen after all and re-opens the whole form family; or (c) a parameter copied to a local at entry, with every use respelled, is numbered as a local rather than coalescing back onto the parameter's register. Reproduce the three probes behind this law on src/game/sys/memcard.c::drawMemCardMessage at commit 0f45ae610; the literal edited text of each is in attempt.RC_drawmemcardmessage-param-block-is-invariant-and-no-bijection-exists.20260902.v1 under probed_form.
subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value:
SCOPE. This BOUNDS claim.law.MV_callee-saved-numbering-has-a-width-class-ahead-of-declaration-order.20260902.v1 from the parameter side. MV establishes that MWCC partitions LOCALS by width, narrow ahead of word-sized, with declaration order operating only within a class, and that the retype across the width boundary is the free lever. Everything MV says is confirmed here. What MV could not see is that its partition covers locals ONLY.

THE RULE. THE ENTRY-COPIED PARAMETER BLOCK IS ITS OWN PARTITION, IT MOVES AS A UNIT, AND NO SOURCE CONSTRUCT REACHES ITS POSITION RELATIVE TO THE LOCALS. Measured on game/sys/memcard.c::drawMemCardMessage, a count-symmetric 204/204 function whose four parameters (msg, options, count1, count2) are copied out of r3-r6 in the first four instructions after the frame setup. The target numbers them r28/r29/r30/r31 - the top of the bank, allocated first descending from r31. Our build numbers them r22/r23/r24/r25 - the bottom, immediately above the two values both builds agree on. Three distinct mechanisms were spent trying to move them:

  DEFINITION FORM IS A CATEGORICAL NULL. Rewriting the definition in K&R old-style, with the four parameters declared in a separate declarator list between the parameter-name list and the opening brace, produced a BYTE-IDENTICAL object. MWCC canonicalises the K&R declarator list to the prototype form in the front end, so the construct never reaches the allocator's decision point. This is the strongest kind of negative - not a failed cure but a demonstration that the lever cannot reach the decision - and it retires the whole definition-form family, prototype-presence variants included.

  THE WIDTH LEVER MOVES LOCALS AND ONLY LOCALS. Retyping the local `int lineH` to `u8 lineH` moved it UP from r27 to r30 exactly as MV predicts, and displaced a sibling local (blit r29 -> r28) with it. The four parameter copies stayed at r22/r23/r24/r25, register for register. The width class is real and operates inside a region that sits entirely below the parameters in our build and entirely above them in the target's - so no amount of local retyping can cross the boundary.

  CONVERTING A PARAMETER TO A LOCAL COALESCES BACK. Adding `s32 sel = count2;` as the last declaration and respelling count2's single use as `sel` DID reach codegen - the object bytes changed, unlike the K&R probe - but the copy coalesced onto count2's existing register, the parameter block held at r22-r25, and the raw differing-word count did not move by a single word (61 before, 61 after).

  A FOURTH MECHANISM IS UNAVAILABLE BY CONSTRUCTION, not merely untried: retyping a PARAMETER is an ABI change, so the free retype MV relies on has no parameter-side analogue at all. C offers no way to declare a parameter relative to a local, and the ABI fixes the parameters' order among themselves.

WHAT THIS PREDICTS, and it is the cheap part to use. When a target-to-ours callee-saved correspondence shows the parameter block sitting at a different HEIGHT in the two banks with the locals' internal structure otherwise intact, do not spend probes on declaration order, initialiser position, scope, definition form or local width - all five are now measured against this boundary. Read the parameter block's position as a fact about the allocator's node ordering and go looking for a lever that changes the LIVE RANGES (call structure, an eliminated or added callee-saved value) or record the function source-exhausted on the numbering axis.

MEASUREMENT NOTE, and a bound on MV's freeness clause reached INDEPENDENTLY of the MV lane's own run-39 refinement. MV v1 states the narrow retype leaves the instruction stream unchanged because MWCC emits the same truncating mask either way. Measured here: retyping `int lineH` to `u8` added one `clrlwi r30,r20,24` and took the function to 205 instructions against the target's 204, because lineH is produced by an int-returning call (`FontHeight(...) + 3`) rather than by a truncating assignment - there is no mask MWCC was already emitting for the retype to reuse. The MV lane's own run-39 refinement states the boundary from the other end, that the retype is free only when the narrow local's USES truncate. The two observations are complementary halves of one condition and were reached by separate lanes on separate functions: the retype is free exactly when a truncation already exists in the stream for it to coalesce with, whether that truncation sits at the definition or at the uses. Treat neither half as the whole rule, and check for an existing mask before predicting a retype is free.
